standard.title: Sustain interactions in varied contexts
standard.description: initiate and sustain interactions in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts to exchange ideas, opinions and experiences about their own and others' personal worlds
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can interact using modelled language to exchange personal information in familiar contexts and manage classroom language (AC9LS8EC01, AC9LS8EC02). They have not yet initiated and sustained interactions independently or exchanged opinions and personal experiences in unfamiliar contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students initiate and sustain interactions in the target language in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts, exchanging ideas, opinions and personal experiences about their own and others' worlds, using strategies to maintain flow and authenticity.

nodes.label: Initiating conversations and topics
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can initiate conversations in the target language using appropriate opening strategies and introduce a topic for discussion.
nodes.minimum_width: Initiate at least one conversation in the target language using an appropriate opening and introduce a topic unprompted.
nodes.typical_width: Use a range of conversation-opening strategies across social and learning contexts; introduce topics with natural, contextually appropriate openers; use small talk strategies to open and maintain early interaction.
wider: Initiate a conversation in an unfamiliar or semi-formal context (e.g. with an older speaker, in a simulated professional context) using appropriate register
Compare conversation-opening conventions in the target language community with Australian English — identify where culturally specific openers are expected

response_modes.reason: Conversation initiation requires a bank of opening strategies across contexts. Students who have only one rehearsed opener will stall in novel situations. Varied practice across social and topic contexts builds the flexibility needed.

success_criteria: Can initiate a conversation in the target language unprompted, using at least one natural opening strategy
Can introduce a topic for discussion without relying on a scripted or heavily modelled prompt

nodes.label: Sustaining interaction and managing flow
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can sustain an interaction in the target language using strategies to maintain flow, show interest and respond to others — including in some unfamiliar contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Sustain a conversation for at least three meaningful exchanges using at least one strategy to maintain flow (e.g. asking a follow-up question, acknowledging a partner's point).
nodes.typical_width: Use active listening, acknowledgement, follow-up questions and spontaneous interjections to maintain authentic conversational flow; manage breakdowns using repair strategies; sustain interactions across familiar and some unfamiliar topics.
wider: Participate in a discussion on a topic introduced spontaneously by a partner — adapt strategies to an unfamiliar topic in real time
Reflect on own conversation strategies after a recorded interaction — identify where flow was lost and what repair strategy could have been used
nodes.hinge_reason: Sustaining interaction is the structural demand of EC01 — it is what distinguishes a scripted exchange from genuine conversation. Students who can initiate but not sustain will be unable to engage with the opinion exchange and experience-sharing demands in nodes 3–4. All collaborative speaking tasks in EC02 and EC03 depend on sustained interaction capacity.

response_modes.reason: Conversation maintenance strategies must be practised across varied partner and topic combinations before they become automatic. Scripted role-play is insufficient — students need semi-structured and unscripted interaction opportunities to develop genuine fluency.
Strategies that work in one familiar conversational context may not transfer to an unfamiliar topic or partner. Varied conversational contexts build transferable interaction skills.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Developing authentic conversation maintenance strategies is central to the oral fluency dimension of the Languages sequence. Students who develop these at Y9-10 have qualitatively different spoken competence — not just more vocabulary, but genuine interactional capacity.
success_criteria: Sustains a conversation for at least three meaningful exchanges without reverting to English or falling silent
Uses at least one active maintenance strategy (follow-up question, acknowledgement, spontaneous response) during the interaction

nodes.label: Exchanging opinions and personal experiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can express and exchange opinions, compare views and share personal experiences in the target language, including on topics of personal and social relevance.
nodes.minimum_width: Express and briefly justify at least one opinion on a familiar topic in the target language; respond to a partner's opinion with agreement or reasoned contrast.
nodes.typical_width: Express, compare and explain opinions and preferences; share and respond to personal experiences; discuss topics of personal and social relevance using structures for agreement, contrast and justification.
wider: Discuss a contentious or socially relevant topic — use persuasion and acknowledgement strategies to manage divergent views respectfully
Share and compare experiences across cultural contexts — identify where experiences or values differ between own background and target language communities

response_modes.reason: Expressing justified opinions requires students to move beyond 'I like/I don't like' to reasoning structures ('because', 'in my opinion', 'on the other hand'). Explicit modelling of opinion structures and supported opinion exchanges scaffold this move.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Opinion exchange across topics of social and personal relevance is where language use becomes genuinely communicative — students are using the target language to do something that matters to them. This is the highest-value interaction context in the Y9-10 strand.
success_criteria: Expresses at least one opinion with a simple justification in the target language
Responds to a partner's contrasting view with a reasoned reply rather than only agreement or silence
